summary:
Antheia is a satellite-based agricultural monitoring platform developed by Team ORBIT IQ. It uses NASA–ISRO NISAR L-band radar data to analyse changes in agricultural land across Faisalabad District, Pakistan. The platform compares HH and HV radar backscatter observations captured 12 days apart to help users explore temporal and spatial patterns in the study area.

Developed using Python, Flask, JavaScript, Leaflet, and geospatial technologies, Antheia provides an interactive dashboard featuring radar visualisations, location-based investigations, district statistics, and temporal comparisons. Its purpose is to make complex satellite data more accessible and support data-informed agricultural monitoring. The project also emphasises scientific reliability by comparing common valid pixels and explaining the limitations of radar measurements. Antheia is designed as a foundation for future enhancements, including advanced geospatial analysis and AI-assisted agricultural insights.
details:
ANTHEIA – Satellite Intelligence for Agricultural Monitoring

Developed by: ORBIT IQ
Study Area: Faisalabad District, Punjab, Pakistan

1. What does our project do, and how does it work?

Antheia is a satellite-based agricultural monitoring and Earth observation platform that uses NASA–ISRO NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) satellite observations to investigate spatial and temporal changes in radar backscatter across Faisalabad District, Pakistan.

The project processes L-band radar observations using two polarization channels: HH (Horizontal-Horizontal) and HV (Horizontal-Vertical). It compares observations from two acquisition dates, 30 October and 11 November 2026, to identify variations in radar backscatter across the study area.

The platform transforms processed satellite data into an interactive web dashboard. Users can explore the geographical boundaries of Faisalabad District, select specific locations to retrieve radar measurements, visualize HH and HV backscatter maps, compare observations across dates, and examine district-level statistical results.

Antheia also includes an integrated Science Desk, which explains important radar concepts through interactive questions and answers. It features a project conclusion and a Scientific Investigation Board covering temporal backscatter analysis, polarization comparison, and spatial data reliability.

The system follows a Python Flask-based architecture, connecting processed satellite data with an interactive frontend developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

2. What benefits does our project have?

Antheia offers several benefits:

  • Accessible satellite data: Converts complex radar observations into understandable visualizations and statistical information.
  • Geographical exploration: Allows users to investigate selected locations within Faisalabad District and retrieve corresponding radar measurements.
  • Temporal monitoring: Helps identify variations in radar backscatter between different satellite acquisitions.
  • Scientific understanding: Explains radar polarization, backscatter, L-band observations, and temporal differences through the Science Desk.
  • Data-driven investigation: Combines geographical information, statistical measurements, and satellite imagery in one platform.
  • Educational value: Provides students and researchers with a practical environment for understanding remote sensing and Synthetic Aperture Radar applications.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact of Antheia is to demonstrate how satellite-based Earth observation can support agricultural and geographical investigations.

By making processed radar observations accessible through an interactive interface, the project aims to encourage the use of remote sensing technologies for understanding changes in agricultural landscapes.

Antheia establishes a foundation for future agricultural monitoring systems that could incorporate additional satellite observations, vegetation indices, soil-moisture estimation methods, and machine learning techniques.

Ultimately, the project aims to bridge the gap between complex satellite data and practical scientific interpretation, particularly in agricultural regions where reliable environmental monitoring can be valuable.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did we use?

The project was developed using the following technologies:

Programming Languages

  • Python – Backend development and data processing.
  • JavaScript – Interactive dashboard functionality and dynamic content updates.
  • HTML5 – Frontend structure.
  • CSS3 – Dashboard styling and responsive design.

Frameworks and Libraries

  • Flask – Python-based web application framework.
  • Leaflet.js – Interactive geographical mapping.
  • Turf.js – Geospatial calculations and geographical boundary validation.

Data and Geospatial Technologies

  • NASA–ISRO NISAR Level-2 GCOV observations.
  • L-band SAR data.
  • HH and HV polarization measurements.
  • GeoJSON – Geographical boundary representation.
  • CSV – Statistical data storage and exchange.

Development Software

  • Visual Studio Code – Development environment.
  • Git and GitHub – Version control and project management.
  • Web browser – Dashboard testing and visualization.

The project uses software-based processing and visualization. No specialized physical hardware is required for the current prototype.

5. How is our project creative and innovative?

Antheia goes beyond simply displaying satellite images. Its creativity lies in combining satellite data processing, geographical exploration, scientific interpretation, and interactive learning within a single platform.

Several features make the project distinctive:

  • Interactive location investigation: Users can select a geographical location on the district map and retrieve its corresponding HH and HV radar observations.
  • Dual-polarization analysis: The platform allows users to explore and compare two complementary radar polarization channels.
  • Temporal visualization: Users can switch between individual acquisition maps and temporal difference maps to investigate changes.
  • Integrated Science Desk: Instead of presenting numerical results without context, Antheia explains the scientific principles behind the measurements through an interactive question-and-answer system.
  • Scientific Investigation Board: The project organizes its analysis into three research investigations, connecting the technical workflow with the questions being explored.
  • Cinematic interface: An animated Earth introduction and a carefully designed dark dashboard create an engaging Earth-observation experience.

The combination of analytical functionality and scientific education makes Antheia both a monitoring prototype and an interactive learning platform.

6. What factors did our team consider during development?

Our team considered several important factors while designing and developing Antheia:

Scientific Accuracy: We aimed to explain radar measurements correctly and distinguish observed backscatter changes from conclusions about actual agricultural conditions.

Data Reliability: Quality masking and common valid pixels were considered important for improving the consistency of temporal comparisons.

Geographical Accuracy: The Faisalabad District boundary was incorporated to ensure that geographical investigations remained within the intended study area.

Usability: The interface was designed to make technical satellite observations accessible through interactive maps, visual comparisons, statistical tables, and understandable explanations.

Performance and Integration: We used a Flask-based architecture to connect the frontend with processed data and backend endpoints while keeping the application modular.

Scalability: The platform was designed with opportunities for future integration of additional satellite observations, analytical methods, and machine learning capabilities.

Scientific Limitations: We considered the fact that radar backscatter is influenced by multiple environmental and surface factors. Therefore, the project does not claim to independently determine crop health or soil moisture from backscatter differences alone.

Conclusion

Antheia demonstrates the potential of combining Earth observation, Synthetic Aperture Radar, geospatial analysis, and interactive web development to investigate agricultural landscapes.

By transforming complex NISAR observations into an accessible analytical platform, ORBIT IQ aims to make satellite-based scientific investigation more understandable, engaging, and useful for future agricultural monitoring applications.

ANTHEIA — Observe. Analyze. Understand.
